Name: Hallows_Eve_Gravekeeper_Restless
$Comment: The Gravekeeper's full moon conversation, what pressing F on him opens in the Forgotten Temple on a
full moon outside Hallow's Eve (his placement NpcPlacements/Hallows_Eve_Gravekeeper_Restless_Temple.json).
During Hallow's Eve his other placement stands him there with his Hallow's Eve conversation
(Hallows_Eve_Gravekeeper.json), so nothing here is ever offered then. He speaks as he always does:
he never contracts.
Every visit opens on greeting: the dead are restless under the full moon, putting down skeletons
and zombies while it is up earns favor with the Hallowed (the Undead row in
Reputations/HallowsEvePack/Hallows_Eve_Hallowed.json), and the graveyard behind him will not stay
quiet: what it costs to go in and what waits there. Its lines are the way in, who he is (the same
words as his Hallow's Eve who screen) and goodnight; the who screen carries gk_back, back to the
greeting or goodnight. The who and goodnight lines reuse his Hallow's Eve conversation's keys, so a
translation covers both.
THE WAY IN. Lay the restless dead to rest is the Dungeon destination for the restless graveyard
(Dungeons/Seasons_Of_Orbis_Restless_Graveyard.json, an endless run of the dead with the Voidtaken
Horseman every fifth wave), which sends the player in with their party, or says why it refused. Its
EntryCost takes five bone fragments from whoever opens an area for their party, and an Eternal Candle
opens it without being spent: picking the line opens CommonLib's confirm screen in this page's place,
with the graveyard's name and description, the fragments, how many the player holds and how many it
takes, and nothing is spent until they confirm. A partymate following into a graveyard their party
already holds skips the screen and walks in free. Option labels take no number from the file, so a
changed count is written into the label and the greeting in every language.
The placement's Season is the only gate; the line asks nothing more. To add a line, put it in
gk_greeting before goodnight. The trick-or-treat line never lands here, since its Season is Hallow's
Eve, and Harvest Feast's invitation line leaves this conversation out by name.
